$comment: The authoritative GSAP pin. Ten authored <script> tags carry this version and hash as
literals — a template is copied verbatim into a generated project, so it cannot read a
variable. Single-sourcing therefore means naming the authority, not removing the copies:
test/unit/test_gsap_pin.py holds every copy to this file.
Why it matters: the integrity hash and the version must correspond. If they do not, the
browser refuses the script, every scene renders with no animation, and nothing in the
authoring loop says so — `npx hyperframes check` catches it only at the Phase 4/5 gate.
The same applies to crossorigin: a cross-origin script carrying `integrity` needs
crossorigin="anonymous" or it never loads at all.
To bump: change `version` here, recompute `integrity` with the command below, propagate
to every authored site, then run `bash test/run.sh`. CI additionally re-fetches the
pinned version and recomputes the hash, which is the one check that needs the network.

excluded.example/index.html: A record of a render that happened, so it stays on the version it was rendered against. Forcing it to track a bump would edit a record to satisfy a lint.
excluded.CHANGELOG.md: Append-only history: an entry describes the tree at release time and is not restated when the pin moves.
